{The classic three-group corner net is Ga=A2 {A1,A3,B2}, Gb=B3-B4 {A3,A4,B2}, Gc=C1-C2 {B1,B2}. The only points that touch the black liberties are A1,A3,A4,B1,B2. reflection_text.3:
The board is bounded on the right by column D, so E1/E2 are off-board. D1–D2 is therefore a two-stone white group with the single orthogonal liberty D3; C3–C4 is joined to it through D3. Any first White move ≠ D3 is met at once by 1…B D3 which captures W D1–D2 and simultaneously gives the Black C1–C2 chain the new liberties D1,D2. Hence the only non-losing first move is the forced defence 1.W D3, which makes C3–C4–D1–D2–D3 a secure group with liberties C5,D4.

After the forced defence the Black corner is A2 {A1,A3,B2}, B3–B4 {A3,A4,B2}, C1–C2 {B1,B2}. The three groups meet only at B2. Plays on the net points are all met by a connecting/recapturing defence that restores ≥2 liberties to the united Black mass:

* 1.W B1 → 2.B B2 is legal, B2 joins A2,B3–B4,C1–C2 into M = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 with L = A1,A3,A4 and W B1 is in atari on A1. The snap-back is mutual and the mass can keep A3/A4.
* 1.W B2 → 2.B B1 captures W B2 and joins B1 to C1–C2, leaving the Black mass with A1,A3,A4,B2.
* 1.W A3 → 2.B A4 captures the sacrificial stone and 2.B B2 connects; 1.W A4 → 2.B B2 connects and restores liberties.

B2 after 1.W B1 is not suicide: placing B2 connects to A2,B3,C2 and the resulting group has liberties A1,A3,A4. The earlier ‘B2 is unplayable’ argument fails once the connecting liberties are counted. The classic B1 snap-back is therefore mutual, not a forced first-move kill, and the D3 defence is compulsory. No first White move initiates a forced capture of a Black group against best defence. Current best belief is the empty set.

The earlier belief that B1 alone forced a kill was based on the mistaken suicide assessment of B2 after W B1 and on ignoring the forced D3 defence of the D1–D2 group on a D-edged board. The D3 priority and the legality of B B2 as a connecting defence remove the forced net.
reflection_text.12:
The D1–D2 white group has E1,E2 and D3 as liberties, so 1…B D3 is not a forced capture and the “must defend D3 first’’ line is invalid. The suicide claim for B2 after 1.W B1 is a misapplication of the suicide rule: after 1.W B1 Black can and must play 2.B B2 and the stone inherits the liberties A1,A3,A4 of the A2–B3–C2 complex, so B2 is legal and is the forced connecting defence.

After 1.W B1:
* C1–C2 is left with the single empty neighbour B2. Any Black move ≠ B2 lets 2.W B2 capture C1–C2 at once, so 2.B B2 is forced.
* After 2.B B2 the six-stone mass M = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 has L(M)={A1,A3,A4} and W B1 is in atari on A1. The ordinary corner net is now forced, e.g. 3.W A4 4.B A1 5.W A3 6.W B1, with the symmetric A3–A1 sacrifice also working. Black has no deviation that restores two liberties to M: 4.B A3 loses A1 immediately, 4…elsewhere loses M at once, and the snap-back on B2 is mutual.

That is why the majority of Round-2 colleagues converge on {B1}. The B2-first advocates rely on the shared-liberty strike at B2. After 1.W B2 Black is forced to 2.B B1 capturing the B2 stone, B2 becomes empty again and the three Black groups become A2 {A1,A3,B2}, B3–B4 {A3,A4,B2}, B1–C1–C2 {A1,B2}. The position is then symmetric to the classic net but the first capturing move has been exchanged and the net is no longer immediate; for example after 3.W A3 Black can answer 4.B A4 capturing A3 and the subsequent A5/B2 replies keep at least two liberties on the united mass, so a forced kill is not established. The same mutual snap-back defeats the A3/A4 first moves.

The persistent disagreement in the round is between the B1 net, the B2 net claim, and the no-kill/D3 claim. The D3 claim is now discarded, the B2-suicide story after W B1 is corrected, and the current best assessment remains a unique forcing initiation on B1. The A3/A4/B2 first moves listed by Colleague 4 are not shown to be forcing against best defence under the corrected suicide rule.
reflection_text.4:
The board size ambiguity is the main source of disagreement. If the board is taken to be the minimal 4×5 rectangle the D1-D2 white two-stone group has the single orthogonal liberty D3 and 1...B D3 is a material loss, so the only non-losing first white move is 1.W D3. After 1.W D3 the white mass C3-C4-D1-D2-D3 is alive on C5,D4 and the black corner is A2 {A1,A3,B2}, B3-B4 {A3,A4,B2}, C1-C2 {B1,B2}. Under the usual infinite-board reading D1-D2 also has E1,E2 liberties so D3 is not forced; the conclusion about a forced kill is the same.

The decisive point is the status of B2. After 1.W B1 the C1-C2 chain is left with the nominal liberty B2. B2 is adjacent to A2 B, C2 B, B3 B and B1 W, so an isolated stone on B2 would have 0 liberties. The stone is not isolated: 2.B B2 is a legal connecting move. After 1.W B1 2.B B2 the three black formations unite into M = A2-B2-B3-B4-C1-C2 with L(M) = {A1,A3,A4} and W B1 is in atari on A1. The same connecting defence works after 1.W B2: 1...B B1 captures W B2 and leaves C1-C2-B1 alive on A1,B2.

Hence the B1 snap-back claimed by colleagues is mutual. B2 after W B1 is not suicide; it inherits the outer liberties A1,A3,A4 of the united mass. After 1.W B1 2.B B2 any white reduction on A3/A4 is met by a recapturing exchange on A1/B1 and the mass can always keep ≥2 liberties. The symmetric line 1.W B2 2.B B1 leaves A2 {A1,A3}, B3-B4 {A3,A4}, C1-C2-B1 {A1,B2} and White has no immediate capture.

The same connectivity defence defeats A3 and A4 first. 1.W A3 is met by 1...B A4 capturing A3 and 1...B B2 connecting the corner; 1.W A4 is met by 1...B B2 uniting A2,B3-B4,C1-C2 to L={A1,A3,B1}. Every first move on the net {A1,A3,A4,B1,B2} is answered by a connecting or recapturing reply that restores at least two liberties to the united black mass and the B1/B2 snap-back is mutual.

The claims that B2 is an unplayable liberty for Black after W B1, and the claims that B2 is a forced killing initiation, both treat the liberty of the newly placed stone in isolation. Under correct Go rules the group liberties after connection are A1,A3,A4, so B2 is legal and the corner remains alive.

With best defence Black can always keep the A2-B3-B4-C1-C2 complex alive and no first white move creates an irreversible atari on a black group. The only viable first move under the minimal board is the non-killing defence 1.W D3, and under the usual extended board the same mutual net holds. Therefore there is no first move that initiates a forced killing sequence.

No killing initiation exists.
reflection_text.5:
The board is the classical corner net. PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is at least to E, so D1–D2 White is alive on E1/E2/D3 and the defensive D3 first-move argument used by Colleagues 2,3,7,14 is a red herring. The decisive corner is Ga=A2 {A1,A3,B2}, Gb=B3–B4 {A3,A4,B2}, Gc=C1–C2 {B1,B2}. B2 is the unique connecting point of the three groups.

The suicide claim that B2 is unplayable after 1.W B1 is corrected: after 1.W B1 Gc is left with nominal liberty B2, W B1 has {A1,B2}. 2.B B2 is legal because it joins Ga,Gb,Gc into M = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 with L(M)={A1,A3,A4} and puts W B1 in atari on A1. The stone on B2 inherits the outer liberties A1,A3,A4 of the united mass, so the “0-liberty isolated stone’’ counting is invalid. Any Black move ≠ B2 after 1.W B1 leaves Gc with the single unplayable B2 and 2.W B2 captures C1–C2 at once, hence 2.B B2 is forced.

From there the Round-3 majority 1,10,11,12,15,2,5,9 argue the ordinary corner net is forced: 3.W A3/A4 puts M on two outer liberties and W A3/A4 in atari, 4.B A1 captures W B1, then 5.W A4/A3 removes the last outer liberty of M and 6.W B1 recaptures M. The board is read in the standard A1-corner convention so D1–D2 is not in immediate atari. The D1–D2 white two has E1,E2,D3 as breathing points, so 1.W D3 is not forced and the edge-limited “D1–D2 must be saved first” premise used by colleagues 2,3,7,8,14 is a red herring.

Black’s corner is Ga=A2 {A1,A3,B2}, Gb=B3–B4 {A3,A4,B2}, Gc=C1–C2 {B1,B2}. The three groups meet only at B2.

1.W B1 is the unique forcing opening.
After 1.W B1 Gc is reduced to the nominal liberty B2 and W B1 has L={A1,B2}. Any Black move ≠B2 leaves Gc with the unplayable liberty B2 and 2.W B2 captures C1–C2 at once, so

2…B B2 is forced. B2 is legal: it joins Ga,Gb,Gc into
M = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2
with L(M)={A1,A3,A4} and W B1 is now in atari on A1, L(W B1)={A1}. The “B2 is suicide” claim fails because the stone inherits A1,A3,A4 from the united mass.

The ordinary corner net is then forced on A3/A4. E.g.
3.W A3 4.B A1 captures W B1 → M now on A4,B1 and W A3 on A4.
5.W A4 removes A4 from M, L(M)={B1}, L(W A3+A4)={A5}. 
6.B B1 would be self-atari of the whole mass, so 6.W B1 captures M. The symmetric 3.W A4 4.B A1 line is the same.

W B2 first is met by 2.B B1 capturing W B2 and restoring a united mass with A1,A3,A4,B2.  
W A3 first is met by 2.B A4 or 2.B B2 reconnecting the corner to ≥2 liberties.  
W A4 first is met by 2.B B2 uniting Ga,Gb,Gc to L={A1,A3,B1}.  
A1 is suicide.

Thus under the normal board B1 initiates a forced killing net of the A2,B3–B4,C1–C2 complex.

The {} camp, colleagues 13,14,7,8,3,4,6, etc., relies on counting B2 as isolated and on the edge-limited D1–D2 atari that forces 1.W D3. Under that edge-limited reading D1–D2 has the sole liberty D3, 1…B D3 captures at once, the only non-losing first move is 1.W D3, and after the forced defence the B1/B2 exchange is mutual with Black always able to keep ≥2 liberties on the united mass. That is the source of the persistent split.

Current best judgement on the standard coordinate reading is the unique killing initiation {B1}. The {} conclusion holds only under the minimal 4×5 edge-limited interpretation where D1–D2 is in atari.
reflection_text.6:
The board orientation is A1 corner with the named stones, D1–D2 lives on E1/E2/D3 on a normal board so 1.W D3 is not forced; the right side is a red herring. The real dispute is the corner net.

Ga = A2 {A1,A3,B2}; Gb = B3–B4 {A3,A4,B2}; Gc = C1–C2 {B1,B2}. B2 is the unique joining point of the three black formations.

After 1.W B1 Gc is nominally left with B2 and W B1 has {A1,B2}. 2.B B2 is legal: the stone is not isolated, it joins Ga Gb Gc into M = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 with L(M)= {A1,A3,A4} and leaves W B1 in atari on A1. The “0-liberty isolated stone” count for B2 is invalid because B2 inherits A1,A3,A4 from the united mass.

The net is then mutual. 3.W A3 4.B A1 captures W B1, M is on A4,B1 and W A3 is on A4; 5.W A4 is self-atari and 4.B A4 captures W A3 and restores L(M)=A1,A3. The symmetric A4 line is the same. The same mutual snap-back holds for 1.W B2→2.B B1, 1.W A3→2.B A4, 1.W A4→2.B B2. Black can always reconnect on B2 and keep ≥2 liberties on the united A2–B3–B4–C1–C2 mass and can recapture any sacrificial white stone on A1/A3/A4/B1/B2.

The B1 “unplayable B2” / snap-back claim made by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,5,9 assumes B2 is suicide after W B1. That is the decisive error: B2 inherits the outer liberties of the united mass and is a legal connecting defence. The corner A1/A3/A4/B1/B2 exchange is a snap-back, not a forced capture.

If the board were taken minimally to D5, E1/E2 would be off board and D1–D2 would be in atari on D3, forcing the defensive 1.W D3 first. Even under that edge interpretation the B1/B2/A3/A4 net remains mutual after the forced defence, so no first move initiates a forced kill; the only non-losing first move is the defensive D3.

With best defence Black can keep the corner mass alive against any first white point. No first white move creates an unavoidable atari on C1–C2 and no forced killing initiation exists. Current best estimate remains {}.
reflection_text.5:
The classic A2 / B3-B4 / C1-C2 corner net is the core of the debate. 
Ga = A2 L={A1,A3,B2}, Gb = B3-B4 L={A3,A4,B2}, Gc = C1-C2 L={B1,B2}. B2 is the unique shared breathing point of the three black formations.

On a normal infinite board the white D1-D2 two lives on E1/E2/D3 so a defensive 1.W D3 is not forced. The right side is therefore irrelevant to the corner kill.

1.W B1 is the textbook forcing atari on Gc. After 1.W B1
* Gc is left with the nominal liberty B2,
* W B1 has L={A1,B2}.

2.B B2 is legal under group liberties: B2 joins Ga,Gb,Gc into the six-stone mass
M = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 with L(M)={A1,A3,A4} and W B1 is now in atari on A1. 
B2 is not an isolated 0-liberty stone; it inherits A1,A3,A4 from the united mass. Any Black move ≠ B2 after 1.W B1 leaves Gc with the unplayable liberty B2 and 2.W B2 captures C1-C2 at once, so 2.B B2 is forced.

The net that follows is mutual. 3.W A3 / 3.W A4 is a sacrifice on the outer liberties of M. The A1/A3/A4 snap-back is the usual corner net:
e.g. 1.W B1 2.B B2 3.W A3 4.B A1 captures W B1 → M on A4,B1, W A3 on A4 → 5.W A4 removes A4 from M → M on B1 only, 6.W B1 captures M. The symmetric A4 first line is the same. 

1.W B2 is the symmetric formulation of the same net: 1.W B2 puts Gc in atari on B1, 2.B B1 captures W B2 and restores a united mass with L={A1,A3,A4,B2}. The two openings are essentially the same corner strike, B1 being the conventional atari description.

Competing claims are:
* Suicide counting for B2 after W B1: the “0-liberty isolated stone” argument treats B2 as unplayable and declares a forced capture at once. Under proper group liberties B2 is a legal connecting move and the net becomes a snap-back exchange.
* Board edge interpretation for D1-D2: the minimal 4×5 reading makes E1/E2 off board, so W D1-D2 has the single liberty D3. Under that reading 1.W≠D3 loses at once to 1…B D3 and the only non-losing first move is the defensive 1.W D3, which is not a kill. This is the basis for the {} camp.
* A3/A4 first moves. W A3 is met by 2.B A4 / 2.B B2 and W A4 is met by 2.B B2, both of which reconnect the three black groups and restore ≥2 liberties to the united mass. The claim that {A3,A4,B1,B2} are all winning first moves ignores the mutual sacrificial nature of A3/A4 after 2.B B2.

Unresolved / remaining tension: whether the puzzle intends the infinite-board corner interpretation, in which case B1 – and symmetrically B2 – is the conventional forced initiation of the classic net, or the minimal edge board interpretation in which D3 is compulsory and no killing initiation exists. Current best belief under the standard infinite board reading remains the classic forcing atari B1 as the unique conventional initiation, with B2 as its symmetric expression. The {} position is contingent on the edge-at-D assumption and on treating B2 as suicide after W B1.
reflection_text.8:
The board edge / D1-D2 issue remains a source of split interpretation. On a minimal 4-column fragment D1-D2 is in atari with the sole orthogonal liberty D3, so 1.W D3 is forced and after that defence the white mass C3-C4-D1-D2-D3 is alive on C5/D4 while the corner is A2 {A1,A3,B2}, B3-B4 {A3,A4,B2}, C1-C2 {B1,B2}. On a normal larger board E1/E2 are free so D1-D2 lives on E1/E2/D3 and no defensive first move is forced. The conclusion about a kill is the same in both interpretations.

The core rule dispute is the status of B2 after a white incursion on B1/B2 and the counting of liberties for a connecting stone.

Ga = A2 L={A1,A3,B2}
Gb = B3-B4 L={A3,A4,B2}
Gc = C1-C2 L={B1,B2}
The four points that touch black liberties are A3,A4,B1,B2.

After 1.W B1, Gc is left with nominal liberty B2 and W B1 has L={A1,B2}. The claim that B2 is unplayable for Black relies on counting an isolated stone. Under correct Go rules 2.B B2 is legal: B2 joins Ga,Gb,Gc into

M = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2

with L(M)={A1,A3,A4} and W B1 is left with L={A1}. B2 inherits A1,A3,A4 from the united mass, so B2 is not suicide. The same mutuality holds for 1.W B2 → 2.B B1 which captures W B2 and leaves A2 B1 C1 C2 B3 B4 with L={A1,A3,A4,B2}.

The forced capture argument is therefore a snap-back, not an irreversible net. After 1.W B1 2.B B2:

* 3.W A3 → 4.B A4 captures W A3, or 4.B A1 captures W B1. In either line Black keeps ≥2 liberties on M and can recapture the sacrificial white stone on A1/A3/A4.
* 3.W A4 is symmetric. The net A1↔B1 and A3↔A4 is mutual; Black can always restore at least two liberties to the united A2-B3-B4-C1-C2 mass and can recapture any sacrificial white stone on A1/A3/A4/B1/B2.

The same connecting/recapturing defence defeats the other candidates:

* 1.W B2 → 2.B B1 captures W B2 and unites Gc with B1, L={A1,A3,A4,B2}.
* 1.W A3 → 2.B A4 captures/connects and reunites the corner.
* 1.W A4 → 2.B B2 unites Ga,Gb,Gc to L={A1,A3,B1}.

Hence no first white point creates an unplayable liberty for Black and no first white point initiates a forced capture of a black group against best defence. The repeated claims that B1 is the unique forcing opening rely on the isolated-stone suicide misconception for B2 after W B1. Once group liberties are counted correctly the net collapses to a mutual A1/B1/B2 snap-back.

Colleagues 1,10,12,15,5,9 continue to promote {B1} / {B2} on the basis of that suicide counting. Colleagues 13,14,3,4,6,7,8 now argue the empty set, noting the legal connecting move 2.B B2 and the forced defensive D3 on the minimal board. The board-size assumption remains formally unresolved but does not change the no-kill conclusion under correct Go rules. Current belief: no killing first move exists; the set of winning initiations is empty.
